newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end down on profit-taking.

text.p: The Hong Kong stock market closed lower on Tuesday due to profit-taking in leading shares and some futures-related activity, brokers said.

"If we strip out the decline caused by the HK$2.00 fall in HSBC shares, the market didn't do too badly today," said Conal Sanjana, institutional sales manager at Kerry Securities. "I wouldn't expect this round of profit-taking to be too extended."

The Hang Seng Index finished 70.60 points down at 12,192.17, but about 20 points off its low for the day of 12,172.84. Turnover was a respectable HK$5.53 billion, slightly higher than Monday's HK$5.49 billion.
HSBC Holdings led the market down with the day's largest net loss of HK$2.00 to close at HK$154.50. The share was also the most actively traded with turnover of HK$375.87 million.
Subsidiary Hang Seng Bank was also a net loss leader, marked down HK$1.00 in afternoon trade to HK$89.75.
HSBC and Hang Seng Bank together account for 26.5 percent of the capitalisation of the blue-chip index, one analyst said.

Futures-linked trade ahead of October contracts expiry on Wednesday was seen as a possible dampener on index heavyweights, but volatility was light compared to previous months. Futures were active and focused on rolling over from October to November.
"Futures-related arbitrage has not had too great a downward pressure on the index today," said Alice Lee, technical analyst at Tai Fook Securities.
October futures closed down 53 points at 12,230, but at a premium to the cash market. The November contract closed at 12,238, down 52 points.
Wall Street's overnight loss also cooled sentiment, dealers said. The Dow industrials lost 34 points to 5,973 on Monday.
The finance sector led the index down, chiefly on the sell-off in HSBC and Hang Seng Bank, followed by the commercial and industrial sector.
Swire Pacific and CITIC Pacific both fell HK$0.50 to HK$68.00 and HK$36.60 respectively. Television Broadcasts lost HK$0.20 to HK$26.30.

In the utility sector China Light eased HK$0.10 to HK$35.50. The company will report earnings for the year ended September 1996 on Monday. Hong Kong Telecom, which will report its interim results next Tuesday, fell HK$0.05 to HK$13.40.
In the H share sector Guangshen Railway dropped HK$0.15 to HK$2.90. The company announced on Monday that it would cut ticket prices by an average 20 percent.
